newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says U.S. sowing discord with Gulf Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Iran says U.S. sowing discord with Gulf Arabs.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen was trying to sow discord between Iran and its Gulf Arab neighbours by saying it was a threat to regional security, an Iranian newspaper said on Tuesday.

The English-language Iran News, which often reflects the views of the Iranian Foreign Ministry, said Cohen was trying "to sow again the seeds of discord between Iran and its neighbours on the southern shores of the Persian Gulf".
"The Islamic republic has existed alongside the Arab countries for the last 18 years and not a single shot has been fired at its neighbours from these borders...," it added.
"Tehran was and still is for good neighbourly relations on the basis of non-interference, mutual interest and respect," it said.

Cohen, on a tour of Iran's Gulf Arab neighbours, said on Tuesday the United States was not headed towards a clash with Iran unless the Islamic republic started it and again warned Tehran against any attempt to halt shipping in the oil-rich Gulf.
"What we have tried to do is to indicate to all of our allies that we are here to provide security against that kind of aggression that might be directed towards them," he said.

The United States accuses Iran of sponsoring state "terrorism" -- a charge Iran denies -- and has expressed mounting concern since the 1991 Gulf War about what it describes as Iran's growing military capability and its aims in the area.

Iran opposes the U.S. military presence in the Gulf and says Washington falsely accuses Tehran of threatening regional security in order to scare its Gulf Arab allies into buying more American weapons.
Its leaders, including President-elect Mohammad Khatami, have said that preserving and improving Iran's relations with its Arab neighbours was a foreign policy priority.
